handback.t:
W5 (DESIGN-BIZ) is finished: in a synthetic multi-domain world, retrieval of recurring briefs through the real `ResearchSession` raises graded quality over every fair baseline in 6 of 7 treatment worlds on both held-out sets. Domain-hierarchical routing adds only a small effect. The board entry with the VERIFY REQUEST blocks, rerun commands, numbers and negatives is `C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\g5_board_entry.md`.

I touched only `src/bin/g5_*` and `results/g5_*`. `src/*.rs` is untouched, there are no commits and no new crates or models. The library proposal is in `results/g5_proposed_patch.md`. `cargo test --release --offline --bin g5_study` passes (4 tests).

**What was built**
- **World:** 5 domains x 4 sub-skills (design, business, marketing, plus coding and math as controls), with tags and text tokens per task. Quality is graded in [0,1] and depends on hidden per-agent competence and on whether the right project brief is retrieved.
- **Pools:** agency (10 agents including a design+marketing "creative" agent), generalists, 20-agent big pool, latent-factor pool with cross-domain correlation, and identical agents.
- **Worlds:** 7 treatment worlds, one stress world (`confusable-briefs`) and 3 controls (`ctl-nocontext-design`, `ctl-coding-math`, `ctl-equal-agents`).
- **Feedback:** every arm, baselines included, gets the same graded, delayed feedback.
- **Arms:**
  - Baselines: keyword, eps-greedy, pooled-thompson, hebbian-robust, warm(hebr), guarded-safe (the "plain" default).
  - Treatments: my 3-level hierarchical router `hier`, `session(warm+retr)`, `session(safe+retr)`, and `hier+retr`.
- **Protocol:** tuned on seeds 1-8, held-out 31-60, confirmed on fresh 61-90 with the same frozen tuning. Paired 95% t-CI against the best fair baseline per cell, with Holm correction per family. Reruns are deterministic.

**Rerun** (use the standard PATH and CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-r5):
- `cargo run --release --offline --bin g5_study -- --check` (replica vs the real session, about 3 s)
- `... --bin g5_study -- --out results/g5_study.json` (about 50 s)
- `... --bin g5_study -- --held 61-90 --out results/g5_study_confirm61-90.json`
- `... --bin g5_study -- --sens` (and again with `--held 61-90`) for the sensitivity runs

**Results at H1500 (mean quality over the first 1500 tasks), difference vs best fair baseline, 31-60 | 61-90**
- **Retrieval + reuse in design/business/marketing:** `session(warm+retr)` is a Holm win in 6/7 treatment worlds on both sets. Its gains range from +.044 to +.111 (31-60; +.039 to +.114 on 61-90), for example agency +.101 | +.102, latent-factors +.111 | +.114, big-pool +.046 | +.046.
- **Hierarchical routing plus retrieval:** `hier+retr` wins 7/7 on both sets, for example agency +.107 | +.109.
- **Per-domain (agency, warm to `hier+retr`):** design .566 to .724, business .636 to .765, marketing .589 to .725; coding .836 to .837 and math .829 to .826 are unchanged.
- **Where the gain comes from:** retrieval adds about +.10 on the same router, about 50% of the headroom between perfect routing with no brief and perfect routing with a perfect brief.
- **Hierarchical routing alone:** +.005 to +.014 over tuned warm(hebr), Holm-significant in 5/7 worlds on 31-60 and 4/7 on 61-90. The domain level itself is worth +.005 to +.028 over the same router without it.
- **Sample efficiency:** retrieval reaches 95% of the best baseline's own late quality about 20-50 tasks sooner in some worlds, Holm-significant in a handful. Hierarchical routing alone is not faster.
- **Controls:**
  - Retrieval is bit-identical to no retrieval when context has no value, so "no regression" there is true by construction.
  - `hier` ties the best baseline in `ctl-coding-math` and `ctl-equal-agents`, and is positive but not significant in `ctl-nocontext-design`.
  - `session(safe+retr)` is a Holm loss to the best baseline in `ctl-coding-math` (-.017 | -.023) and in `low-recurrence` (-.018 | -.016). Retrieval is not the cause: guarded-safe is simply 0.01-0.02 worse than warm(hebr) in these graded worlds.

**Negatives**
- The retrieval gain exists because I wrote quality's dependence on a brief into the world. The sensitivity runs show it scales about linearly with that dependence, vanishes with rare project recurrence (200 projects: +.001), and turns slightly negative (-.007 to -.009) when tasks identify their project weakly (1 of 3 tokens).
- Hash embeddings only; the MiniLM fixture cannot embed these synthetic tasks.
- Wrong-brief harm in design reaches -.025 in the low-recurrence and confusable worlds.
- Early cost: `session(warm+retr)` is behind the early leader guarded-safe at H100 by -.058 | -.045 in `confusable-briefs`.
- `hier` is behind best fair by about -.010 to -.020 in the first 100 tasks in 6 of 8 worlds, and is not Holm-significant at H500 on 61-90 (0/7).
- The tuned retrieval knobs (store_min .55, sim_min .75) differ from the library defaults, and I did not run the defaults themselves.
- `hier+retr` runs in an in-bin replica of `run_task`, because the session cannot take a custom router. The replica matches the real session bit-for-bit (max difference 0.0) for the safe and warm routers, with and without retrieval, including the brief-ingest path.
- The critic is off, so no critic claim is made.
